title: NaN Loss / Exploding Gradients
description: Troubleshooting and resolving numerical instability during training, including NaN loss and exploding gradients. This guide provides a structured debugging flow, investigation checklists, and mitigation strategies for stabilizing deep learning models.
name: NaN Loss / Exploding Gradients

quick_identification.check: Loss becomes NaN or inf during training
quick_identification.description: Monitor training logs for nan or inf values in loss.

quick_identification.check: Gradients contain NaN or inf values
quick_identification.description: Inspect gradient tensors or apply gradient norm checks before the optimizer step; clipping utilities can also expose runaway norms.

quick_identification.check: Model weights become NaN after training
quick_identification.description: Validate checkpoints or parameter tensors for non-finite values before save and after optimizer updates.

symptoms.description: Training loss suddenly becomes NaN or infinity, often after a few iterations.
symptoms.error_message: loss: nan or loss: inf in training logs.
symptoms.where_appears: Training loop, loss computation, optimizer step.

symptoms.description: Gradient norms grow rapidly and eventually destabilize optimization.
symptoms.error_message: May not show an explicit error, but training diverges.

symptoms.description: Model produces garbage or highly variable outputs.
symptoms.error_message: No explicit error, but outputs are nonsensical.

root_causes.explanation: Oversized updates push parameters into regions where activations, loss terms, or optimizer state become numerically unstable; gradient clipping theory and practical guidance both treat uncontrolled step size as a major instability driver.
recognition_clues: Reducing learning rate by 10x restores stability.
Failure appears early and reproducibly across seeds.
root_causes.typical_environment: Training with large models, especially transformers.

root_causes.explanation: FP16/bfloat16 arithmetic can overflow or underflow intermediate values, and incorrect scaling or autocast usage can turn finite values into NaN/inf during forward or backward passes.
recognition_clues: NaN appears only when AMP is enabled.
Loss scaling behavior changes the failure point.
root_causes.typical_environment: Mixed precision training with large batch sizes.

root_causes.explanation: Accumulation bugs can effectively apply updates at the wrong scale, compound stale gradients, or skip required zeroing/unscaling steps, which amplifies instability over multiple microbatches.
recognition_clues: NaN appears after multiple accumulation steps.
root_causes.typical_environment: Training loops with manual gradient accumulation.

root_causes.explanation: Invalid or extreme input values can drive activations or loss terms out of range, especially when a specific batch contains NaN/inf, extreme outliers, or malformed labels.
recognition_clues: Validation loss is stable while training fails.

root_causes.explanation: Loss implementations can overflow on extreme logits, invalid probabilities, or poorly bounded regression targets; framework numerics checks exist specifically to catch this class of failure.
recognition_clues: NaN appears in a specific loss function.
Predictions become very large before NaN.
Rewriting the loss in a stable form removes the issue.
root_causes.typical_environment: Classification with extreme logits, regression with outliers.

investigation_checklist.description: Verify the optimizer step size is appropriate for the model, batch size, and schedule.
Log or inspect global gradient norm before the optimizer step to confirm runaway magnitudes.
Verify autocast, loss scaling, and unscale-before-clip ordering are correct.
Inspect batches, labels, and masks for NaN/inf or extreme outliers.
Verify the loss is numerically stable under extreme logits, probabilities, or masks.
Verify momentum, adaptive moments, and scaler state are not corrupted after a failed step.

diagnostic_commands.interpretation: Very large norms indicate exploding gradients; clipping infrastructure also gives a direct hook for mitigation.
Any non-zero count indicates data issues.

diagnostic_tests.test: Run training with 10x smaller learning rate.
diagnostic_tests.expected_result: Stable loss with reduced learning rate.
diagnostic_tests.interpretation: If stable, the learning rate was likely too high.
diagnostic_tests.next_action: Reduce learning rate or use a warmup schedule.

diagnostic_tests.test: Run training without automatic mixed precision.
diagnostic_tests.interpretation: If stable, AMP configuration needs adjustment.
diagnostic_tests.next_action: Adjust AMP settings or use loss scaling.

yes.result: Learning rate too high - reduce by 10x.
Mixed precision instability - disable or adjust.

no.question: Do gradient norms grow over time?
Does NaN appear on specific batches?

no.result: Loss function numerical overflow - add a stable formulation or clipping.

solutions.permanent_fix: Implement a learning-rate scheduler with warmup.
steps: Reduce learning rate by a factor of 10.
Add gradient clipping to contain future spikes.
solutions.performance_impact: Moderate slowdown from extra steps to convergence.

solutions.permanent_fix: Tune clipping threshold against observed gradient distributions.
steps: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ before the optimizer step.
Monitor gradient norms to tune the threshold.
tradeoffs: Can hide an underlying optimizer or data bug.
works_for: Unstable gradients in transformers and RNNs.
solutions.verification: Gradient norms remain below the clipping threshold and loss stops diverging.

solutions.permanent_fix: Use native AMP with proper scaling and unscale-before-clip ordering.
tradeoffs: Slightly reduced throughput versus pure AMP.
solutions.performance_impact: Small throughput reduction relative to unstable mixed-precision runs.
solutions.verification: No NaN appears with AMP enabled, and loss-scaling behavior is stable.

verification_checklist.description: Gradient norms stay within reasonable bounds.
Model quality improves on the validation set.

practices: Profile loss values before scaling to full training.
Set up alerts for NaN/inf in training metrics.
Use learning-rate schedulers with warmup and decay.
Implement automatic restart or job fail-fast on numerical instability.
Stop or quarantine runs on first non-finite value.
Always check for NaN in custom loss functions.
Use numerically stable primitives for softmax, log, and ratio computations.
Add gradient checks in training loops.

common_misconceptions.misconception: NaN always means the model is broken
common_misconceptions.reality: It is often caused by learning rate, AMP, data, or loss formulation issues rather than architecture.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Gradient clipping always fixes exploding gradients
common_misconceptions.reality: It reduces damage but does not remove the underlying root cause.
Too low can cause slow convergence or optimization stagnation.

false_positive_cases.how_to_distinguish: Loss remains finite but does not decrease.
Training loss is stable, validation is increasing.
Actual loss values are valid; logging format is wrong.

escalation_paths.when_to_use: Need to find a stable operating range fast.
tradeoffs: May not generalize across batch sizes.

escalation_paths.when_to_use: Standard optimizers remain unstable after basic fixes.
Single-GPU training remains unstable and scale-out diagnosis is needed.
